topic: The cave sealed from sunlight for 5.5 million years

sections.voiceover: In 1986, workers near the Black Sea broke into a cave that had been sealed for five and a half million years. Inside: toxic air, total darkness, and thirty-five species found nowhere else on Earth.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom from cave entrance darkness into a flashlight reveal. Cool blues, deep blacks.
sections.sfx_cue: Low sub-bass drone fading in. Distant drip echoes.
sections.pacing_notes: First word lands at 0:02. Pause 1 second after the hook.

sections.voiceover: Oxygen at just seven percent. Air thick with hydrogen sulfide. And yet life is everywhere: blind spiders, eyeless leeches, ghost-pale centipedes, none of them needing sunlight to survive.
sections.visual_cue: Macro close-ups of pale cave creatures, bioluminescent glow accents.
sections.sfx_cue: Tight ambient bed, heartbeat-like pulse. Environmental SFX: water drip, breathing.
b_roll: Macro shot of blind cave creature
sections.transition_out: Hard cut to black, 1 second silence
sections.pacing_notes: Deliver first sentence slower, then accelerate through the list.

sections.voiceover: And this cave is not alone. In the deepest caves on Earth, two kilometers down, a springtail called Plutomurus holds the record for the deepest animal ever found: 1,980 meters below the surface, in a world with no light at all.
sections.visual_cue: Vertical descent shots, cross-section cave map animation with depth markers.
sections.sfx_cue: Low tension drone builds. Subtle data-stream blips on the depth counter.
b_roll: Cross-section cave map with depth line
sections.pacing_notes: Let the depth number land. Pause after 1,980 meters.

sections.voiceover: These creatures do not eat sunlight. They eat chemistry: bacteria turning minerals and sulfur into food, exactly like the vents of the deep ocean. Entire ecosystems running on nothing but rock.
sections.visual_cue: Microbial chemistry animation, mineral textures, comparison to deep-sea vents.
sections.sfx_cue: Drone fades to near-silence. Mineral-like chimes as the chemistry concept lands.
sections.pacing_notes: Speed up slightly through the concept, slow down on the final line.

sections.voiceover: So next time you stand in the sun, remember: two kilometers below your feet, life is thriving in a world that has never seen it. Follow Depth Unknown for more from the dark.
sections.visual_cue: Return to cave entrance shot, same framing as the hook, then fade to black.
sections.sfx_cue: Return of opening drone. Swell slightly, then fade to silence.
sections.transition_out: Fade to black. End screen elements appear.
sections.pacing_notes: First sentence mirrors the hook. Understated CTA, one sentence only.
